{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings 

---

## 1. Executive summary

This Agreement is unusually well aligned with our playbook. Of the eighteen rules reviewed, sixteen are compliant, several at our preferred position in full — indemnification (§ 20), IP and Customer Data ownership (§ 14), assignment and change of control (§ 24), licence scope (§ 13), termination for convenience (§ 9.4 / § 29.4), audit (§ 22), governing law and New York venue (§ 28), renewal and CPI/3% uplift cap (§ 8), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), warranties (§ 19) and insurance (§ 18). The Agreement also contains affirmative protections that run in our favour and that we do not disturb: no exclusivity, non-compete, no-hire or minimum-volume commitment (§ 2.1, § 12.3), a Vendor-side competitive restraint (§ 12.4), and a Vendor-granted MFN on Fees (§ 7.6).

Two issues require redlines, and both sit in walk-away territory notwithstanding their low severity rating:

- **§ 7.7 — liquidated damages payable by Customer.** A payment-delay charge of fifteen percent of annual Fees per week, triggered by a ten-day delay, would exceed the remaining contract value in roughly seven weeks. This cannot be brought within our fallback (an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees) because it is not a termination fee at all.
- **§ 21.1 — cap basis.** Mutuality, the consequential-damages exclusions and the Excluded Claims list are all acceptable. The defect is that the cap is measured by Fees under the first Order Form only, and Fees are defined (§ 1.5–1.6) as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee — rendering the cap illusory and well below six months' charges.

Both redlines are drafted as minimal operative changes and leave the surrounding Vendor remedies and liability architecture intact.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 Termination |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 Audit Rights |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8 Term and Renewal |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 Warranties |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance |
| Low | **LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer** | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.7) |
| Low | **LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs** | **Deviation** | § 21 Limitation of Liability (§ 21.1) |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

Both deviations are identified in the findings as walk-away territory:

1. **§ 7.7 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** Fifteen percent of annual Fees per week, triggered by a ten-day payment delay, exceeding remaining contract value within approximately seven weeks. Not capable of falling within the fallback.
   - *Proposed redline:* flip § 7.7 so that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer, leaving Vendor's other late-payment remedies and the § 7.3 interest reference untouched.
2. **§ 21.1 — illusory liability cap.** Cap measured by Fees under the first Order Form only, which per §§ 1.5–1.6 is the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee — well below six months' charges.
   - *Proposed redline:* reset limb (a) to the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000; mutuality, the § 21.2 damages exclusions and the § 21.3 Excluded Claims remain as drafted.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. Issue the two redlines above to Vendor, with short [Playbook] comments explaining that § 7.7 fails our position on Customer-payable liquidated damages and that the § 21.1 cap basis, as defined, is illusory.
2. Confirm with the business the expected annual contract value, so the twelve-month cap basis and the USD 1,000,000 floor in § 21.1 are calibrated correctly before we send.
3. Hold the sixteen compliant positions as drafted — in particular § 20 (indemnities as Excluded Claims), § 14, § 24, § 13, § 9.4/§ 29.4, § 22, § 28, § 8.3, § 11, § 19 and § 18 — and resist any Vendor attempt to reopen them in exchange for the two changes we are seeking.
4. Preserve the Customer-favourable terms in § 2.1, § 7.6, § 12.3, § 12.4 and § 24.4 without amendment.
5. Escalate to the deal principal if Vendor declines either redline, given that both items are flagged as walk-away."}
